note: How quality topics relate. Edges asserting what a test does or does not establish must cite the claim or the recorded gap behind them; the database refuses them otherwise. Structural edges declare themselves navigational and must not smuggle an assertion into the rationale. This is the HPLC hub only — other topics gain their own edges when they gain their own evidence.

edges.rationale: A high purity figure is routinely read as confirmation that the material is what the label says. It is not: chromatography separates, and separation yields no information about covalent structure. Identity is a separate question with its own test.

Purity and amount are different measurements. A preparation can be highly pure and still contain much less peptide than expected, because purity describes the proportions of what was detected, not the mass of peptide in a vial.
Chromatography shows how many species are present; mass spectrometry shows what they weigh, and therefore bears on what they are. The two are designed to be read together.
The same separation that measures how mixed a preparation is, is also how it is purified. Assessment and purification are stages of one cycle rather than separate activities.
Sterility is a microbiological question and chromatography does not address it. This index holds no source on sterility testing, so it records the gap rather than asserting the conclusion.
Bacterial endotoxin is likewise a microbiological attribute of a finished preparation, tested by a method this register holds no source for.
Solvents from synthesis and purification are a separate attribute with their own testing. This index holds no source on that testing yet, so the topic is registered rather than written.
Water content is a separate attribute with its own testing. This index holds no source on it yet, so the topic is registered rather than written.
The pH of a reconstituted solution is a separate attribute with its own measurement. This index holds no source on it yet.
Elemental impurities are a separate attribute with their own testing. This index holds no source on that testing yet, so the topic is registered rather than written.

Every result describes the material that was tested. Which batch that was, and whether it is the batch in hand, is a record-keeping question rather than an analytical one — and it governs how far any result on this page reaches.
